newsitem.title: KENYA: Lack of demand stagnating Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Lack of demand stagnating Nairobi bourse.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) share index gained a mere 0.06 points on Monday and brokers blamed the market stagnation on a lack of investor demand for shares.
The 20-share index gained 0.06 points to stand at 3036.01. Turnover was posted at 9.273 million shillings traded on 284,911 shares from 7.232 million shillings traded on 187,684 shares on Monday.
"With four public offers having gone through this year, the secondary market has been a financial drain on most investors," a broker said.
"Investors do not have any more money," he said.
Rea Vipingo Plantations, national carrier Kenya Airways, National Bank of Kenya and Kenya Commercial Bank have had public share offers this year.

"Normally there is some level of price movement especially when company announcements are about to come, but it is amazing the way the market is just dull. There is no excitement about anything," another broker said.
"I think the market would be good for medium term investors, not speculators," a bourse official said.

Activity concentrated on financials. Some 54,968 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank were traded at 55.50 from 55, National Bank of Kenya traded 81,475 shares at 14.50 unchanged while Barclays Bank was stable at 96.
On average prices on key shares were stable with marginal gains. Sasini Tea & Coffee traded at 53.50 from 53 while oil concern Total Kenya eased to 68.50 from 69.
